summary: Dmitry Medvedev was nominated as the presidential successor by four parties and publicly supported by Vladimir Putin, positioning him to become president in March 2008.
Dmitry Medvedev said he wanted Vladimir Putin to become prime minister after the presidential election.
Vladimir Putin says he would accept the post of prime minister if his close ally Dmitry Medvedev becomes Russia's next president.
The United Russia party unanimously nominated Dmitry Medvedev as its candidate for the March 2 presidential election after Vladimir Putin endorsed him.
Russia's future president Dmitry Medvedev began his election campaign by acknowledging rampant corruption and "legal nihilism" in Russia.
Russian President Vladimir Putin sent likely successor Dmitry Medvedev to Belgrade to supervise the signing of a $1.5bn gas agreement with Serbia.
Dmitry Medvedev is running as a presidential candidate with Vladimir Putin's backing, and the election result is widely expected to make him Russia's next president.
Vladimir Putin urged Russians to vote in the upcoming presidential election in which Dmitry Medvedev was his chosen successor.

The Kremlin is planning to falsify the results of Russia's presidential election by compelling public sector workers to vote and fraudulently boosting turnout to secure a landslide majority for Dmitry Medvedev.
Dmitry Medvedev is elected Russia's next president.
UK Prime Minister Gordon Brown writes to Russian president-elect Dmitry Medvedev to offer congratulations and express hope for repairing strained relations.
President-elect Dmitry Medvedev signals he intends to continue the same hardline policies towards the West as his predecessor Vladimir Putin.
Russian president-elect Dmitry Medvedev warns that Nato membership for Ukraine and Georgia could threaten European security and undermine attempts to improve transatlantic relations.
Financial Times editor Lionel Barber interviewed Russian president-elect Dmitry Medvedev, who said he occasionally reads FT.com.

Vladimir Putin was offered leadership of the United Russia party, a move analysts said would strengthen his position relative to incoming president Dmitry Medvedev, who was to be inaugurated on May 7.
An analysis by physicist Sergei Shpilkin of official results from Russia's central elections committee found statistical anomalies indicating fraud in Dmitry Medvedev's presidential election victory.
Dmitry Medvedev was sworn in as Russia's new president during a ceremony at the Kremlin, succeeding Vladimir Putin.

Dmitry Medvedev, newly inaugurated as president, proposed Vladimir Putin for prime minister and said he would pass a decree formally naming Putin as head of the new government after the State Duma confirmed him.
Dmitry Medvedev flew into Siberia for his international debut, a summit with EU leaders.
Dmitry Medvedev hosted talks between the EU and Russia on a new partnership and cooperation agreement, marking his major international debut as Russia's new president.
Dmitry Medvedev hosts talks between the EU and Russia on a new partnership and cooperation agreement in Khanty-Mansiisk, marking his major international debut as Russia's new president.

In a lengthy Kremlin interview, Russian President Dmitry Medvedev presents himself as a man of "colossal experience" ahead of the G8 summit and discusses Kosovo, Iran sanctions, and reforming the world financial system.
Dmitry Medvedev gives an interview to the Guardian presenting a moderate and reasonable face to the world.

At the G8 summit in Japan, Russian President Dmitry Medvedev took a more pugnacious stance than expected in his first meeting with British Prime Minister Gordon Brown, refusing to budge on issues such as the extradition of Andrei Lugovoi, the closure of British Council offices in Russia, and visa problems for BP staff.

Russia's new president Dmitry Medvedev launched an outspoken attack on America's European missile defence plans, accusing the US of aggravating the situation and promising Russia would respond appropriately.
Russian President Dmitry Medvedev launched an outspoken attack on US European missile defence plans, accusing the US of aggravating the situation and promising Russia would respond appropriately.
Russian President Dmitry Medvedev said it would be "no great loss" if Nato broke off ties with Russia, following the war in Georgia.
Russian President Dmitry Medvedev recognizes the breakaway Georgian provinces of South Ossetia and Abkhazia as independent.

Russia's president Dmitry Medvedev outlined plans for a new European security pact to ban the use of force in Europe and defuse tensions between Moscow and Nato, and promised that by midnight Russian troops would leave "security zones" in the undisputed areas of Georgian territory.
President Dmitry Medvedev proposes extending the Russian presidential term from four to six years and announces the deployment of cruise missiles in western Russia.
Russian President Dmitry Medvedev deploys nuclear missiles in Kaliningrad in response to America's missile and radar system deployment on Russia's border.
Russia's parliament voted to extend the presidential term from four to six years after Dmitry Medvedev abruptly proposed the constitutional amendment.

Dmitry Medvedev marked the first anniversary of his election victory amid a Kremlin power struggle between factions loyal to him and to Vladimir Putin over control of state finances during Russia's financial crisis.
A new trial of jailed tycoon Mikhail Khodorkovsky commences, seen as a chance for President Dmitry Medvedev to demonstrate his commitment to the rule of law.

Barack Obama and Dmitry Medvedev met on the eve of the G20 summit in London and pledged to agree cuts in their countries' nuclear arsenals by December, with Obama accepting an invitation to visit Moscow in July.

President Barack Obama and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev released a joint statement committing the two countries to a three-month goal of negotiating a new, legally-binding arms control treaty, with a long-term goal of "achieving a nuclear free world."
President Dmitry Medvedev gave an interview to the opposition newspaper Novaya Gazeta, in which he defended democracy and the rule of law.
One year has passed since Dmitry Medvedev took over as Russia's president, with observers debating whether he is a genuine reformer or a fake.

Russian President Dmitry Medvedev signaled he could ease political restrictions imposed by his predecessor Vladimir Putin, including possibly lowering the 7% threshold for political parties to win seats in the State Duma.
Dmitry Medvedev unveiled plans to open up regional and national politics to younger Russians, especially those under 30.

Barack Obama says the US is developing a "very good relationship" with Dmitry Medvedev on issues such as nuclear arms reduction, while also criticizing Vladimir Putin's "cold war approaches" ahead of his Moscow trip.
Dmitry Medvedev said he might seek a second term as president, but backed down after Vladimir Putin said they would decide between themselves who would stand in 2012.
Russian President Dmitry Medvedev admitted in his official blog that Russia faces major structural problems, including a weak democracy, shrinking population, and a non-performing economy.

President Dmitry Medvedev announced a major reform programme to clean up corruption in Russia, force oligarchs to share their wealth, and diversify its oil-dependent economy, while hinting he could run for a second term.
Dmitry Medvedev said after meeting Barack Obama that sanctions rarely lead to productive results but in some cases are inevitable, remarks interpreted as a possible shift on Iran sanctions.

Russians vote in regional elections, the first test of President Dmitry Medvedev's pledge to make Russia's electoral system more competitive, amid opposition accusations that the Kremlin fixed the Moscow city election.
In his annual state of the nation address, Russian President Dmitry Medvedev proposed reducing Russia's 11 time zones, though he did not specify how this would work.
Russian President Dmitry Medvedev signed Russia's new military doctrine, which names NATO and the US as the main dangers.

Russia indicated it had reached agreement with the United States on a historic nuclear arms reduction treaty to replace the 1991 Start treaty, with a signing ceremony between Obama and Russia's president Dmitry Medvedev likely to take place early next month in Prague.
Dmitry Medvedev said he outlined Russia's limits on sanctions against Iran during a frank discussion with Barack Obama, calling for smart, targeted measures that would not harm the Iranian people.
Mikhail Gorbachev criticizes President Dmitry Medvedev and Prime Minister Vladimir Putin, accusing them of moving away from democracy and eroding civil liberties to stay in power.
WikiLeaks cables reveal US diplomats believe Vladimir Putin remains Russia's real leader, with Dmitry Medvedev playing a junior role described as "Robin to Putin's Batman."

President Dmitry Medvedev responds to Prime Minister Vladimir Putin's criticism of Western air strikes on Libya by saying it is inadmissible to use expressions like "Crusades" that can lead to a clash of civilizations.

Russian President Dmitry Medvedev unveiled a plan to purge government ministers from the boards of large state companies, setting a 1 July deadline for Prime Minister Vladimir Putin to carry out the ouster.

President Dmitry Medvedev calls for the resignation of all government ministers from state-run firms ahead of shareholder meetings in June, criticizing the government's increasing role in the economy.

A senior United Russia MP says Dmitry Medvedev wants to stay on as Russian president and has broken an agreement with Vladimir Putin, with Medvedev's allies campaigning to undermine Putin ahead of the March 2012 election.
Dmitry Medvedev promises to reveal soon whether he will run for a second term as president of Russia.

Russia's justice ministry barred the liberal opposition People's Freedom party from taking part in forthcoming elections, dealing a blow to President Dmitry Medvedev's attempts to portray Russia as a flourishing democracy.
Russian President Dmitry Medvedev announced he favours stepping back and recommending his predecessor, Vladimir Putin, to succeed him in 2012.

At the United Russia party conference, Dmitry Medvedev accepted Vladimir Putin's proposal that he head the party's federal list in December's parliamentary vote and said he would be ready to become prime minister if the party won, while Putin accepted the presidential nomination.
President Dmitry Medvedev asked Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin to step down after Kudrin refused to serve once Medvedev swapped the presidency with Vladimir Putin in May.
Outgoing Russian President Dmitry Medvedev said he agreed to step down because he believes Vladimir Putin is more popular, and Putin has said he will make Medvedev his prime minister.
Russian President Dmitry Medvedev urged Syrian counterpart Bashar al-Assad to reform or leave office, the first time the allies have publicly diverged during Syria's uprising.

Russian President Dmitry Medvedev proposed liberal electoral reforms, including reinstating gubernatorial elections and easing party registration rules, in an apparent attempt to appease anti-government protesters ahead of a planned demonstration.

Former Kremlin insider Gleb Pavlovsky says growing rivalry between Vladimir Putin and Dmitry Medvedev led Putin to seek re-election as president, leaving Medvedev a lame duck despite being promised the prime minister job.

Russian Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev dismissed warnings at the World Economic Forum in Davos that his government faces a middle class revolt if it does not embrace deeper economic and political reforms, insisting Russia was on the right path and a good place to invest.
Russian Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev criticizes Western recognition of Ukraine's transitional government as an "aberration" and describes the ousting of President Viktor Yanukovych as a "mutiny."
Ukrainian Prime Minister Arseny Yatseniuk urged Russian counterpart Dmitry Medvedev in a phone call to return Russian soldiers to base in Crimea and called for talks.
Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev visits Crimea for a cabinet meeting, promising economic benefits and signaling Russia's intention to retain the annexed territory.
Hackers reportedly accessed Russian Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev's Twitter account and posted hoax tweets, including a fake resignation message, before the account's security was strengthened.
Dmitry Medvedev's United Russia party obtained 44.5% of the vote in Russia's parliamentary elections, according to a state-run exit poll.
Dmitry Medvedev became the main target of large street protests across Russian cities following Alexei Navalny's corruption investigation alleging a network of palaces and vineyards linked to him.
